title: Assure laboratory quality standards and legislative compliance

lessons.title: Quality assurance tasks in the workplace
lessons.html:
From following the system to assuring it

In this workplace module you take an active role in maintaining the laboratory's quality management system, working with the quality manager. You show that you can monitor compliance, find weaknesses and help fix them.

Tasks to perform

  • Document control: check that only current versions of procedures and the current ISTA Rules edition are in use; withdraw obsolete copies.
  • Equipment programme: maintain the calibration and maintenance schedule, review certificates, check that intermediate checks are done and recorded.
  • Environmental monitoring: review germinator and cold room temperature logs; investigate excursions.
  • Training and authorisation records: check that every analyst performing a test is authorised for it.
  • Internal quality control: compile repeat test and control sample results; look for trends between analysts or over time.
  • Proficiency testing: coordinate samples, submit results, review reports and follow up poor performance.
  • Sample retention: check that retained samples are stored correctly and disposed of only after the required period.

Internal audits

Take part in planned internal audits:

  1. Prepare a checklist from the standard and procedures.
  2. Observe work, examine records and interview staff.
  3. Trace a sample from receipt to report to test traceability.
  4. Record findings objectively, with evidence.
  5. Agree corrective actions and deadlines with the responsible person.

Vertical audit example

Pick a reported germination result. Check the sample register, working sample record, analyst authorisation, germinator log for the test period, substrate batch, count sheets, tolerance check, technical review and the issued report. Any gap breaks traceability and is a finding.

lessons.title: Legislative compliance and continual improvement
lessons.html:
Keeping legal requirements current

Maintain a legal and normative register listing the laws, regulations, scheme rules and standards that apply: seed legislation such as the Plant Improvement Act 53 of 1976 and its regulations (confirm with your organisation what is currently in force), certification scheme rules, ISTA Rules and Accreditation Standard, ISO/IEC 17025 where SANAS accreditation is held, and phytosanitary requirements for exports. For each, record the current version, the effective date and who is responsible for applying changes.

Applying changes

  1. Review new ISTA Rules editions and regulatory amendments when published.
  2. Identify which procedures, forms and training are affected.
  3. Update and approve documents before the effective date.
  4. Train staff and record the training.
  5. Verify after implementation that work follows the new requirement.

Managing non-conformities and complaints

Record each non-conformity or complaint, contain it, assess its effect on issued results, find the root cause (for example with the five whys or a cause-and-effect diagram), implement corrective action and verify that it worked. Inform clients when issued results are affected.

External assessments

Help prepare for accreditation assessments and regulatory inspections: ensure records are complete and accessible, close outstanding actions, and brief staff. During assessments, answer honestly and provide evidence promptly. Afterwards, address findings within the deadlines set.

Management review

Contribute data to management review: audit findings, proficiency results, non-conformities, complaints, workload, resource needs and improvement proposals. Management review decides priorities for the coming period.

Evidence for assessment

  • Internal audit checklists and reports you contributed to.
  • Calibration and environmental log reviews.
  • Non-conformity records you handled from detection to closure.
  • Updates to the legal register and associated training records.
  • Mentor or quality manager testimony.

Key points

  • Monitor document control, equipment, environment and authorisations.
  • Use vertical audits to test traceability from sample to report.
  • Keep a current legal and normative register with effective dates.
  • Close non-conformities with root-cause analysis and verified corrective action.
  • Support external assessments and management review with accurate data.
